scenario: [LCST.4.5.8] parses a text as a source INT_LIT or FLOAT_LIT spells it, and [LLEX.11.1] / [LLEX.11.2] admit a `_` only between two digits, one at a time, in the integer part, the fraction and the exponent alike. So a doubled `_` is `null` in each: `1__5.5`, `15.5__0`, `1.55e0__1`. Each control, the same text with one `_`, parses to 15.5. Each text is asserted and pumped on its own, so the log order is the assert order. Rule `absent` logs a text whose `::Float?` is null, and rule `parsed` one that parses to 15.5. PATH PINNED: FN_STRING_TO_FLOAT's runtime adapter, through libds's `digit_run` (`float_text/float_parse.cc`, `ds_parse_float_text`), which the Mercury runtime calls for `String :: Float?` too. The breaks: a parser that skips a doubled `_` in any of the three digit runs logs `15.5 [...]` in place of that text's `null [...]`; one that refuses every `_` logs `null [...]` for a control.
rules_ds:
schema S scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    txt: String mutable

rule absent:
    S s where (s.txt::Float?) is null
->
    log info "null [{s.txt}]"

rule parsed:
    S s where (s.txt::Float? ?? 0.0) == 15.5
->
    log info "15.5 [{s.txt}]"
